question.:question/problem: Find $f(x,y)$ such that $∇f=F,$ where $F(x,y)=(- 4 y - 4 \cos{\left(x + y \right)})\,i+(- 4 x - 4 \cos{\left(x + y \right)})\,j.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the function $f(x,y)$ is defined as

$$
∇f(x,y)=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\,i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\,j.
$$

Since $∇f(x,y)=F(x,y),$ the function $f(x,y)$ must satisfy the following system:

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=- 4 y - 4 \cos{\left(x + y \right)},\qquad \frac{∂f}{∂y}=- 4 x - 4 \cos{\left(x + y \right)}.
$$

First, we integrate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ with respect to $x.$ Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y)&=\int \frac{∂f}{∂x}\,\text{d}x\\&=\int (- 4 y - 4 \cos{\left(x + y \right)})\,\text{d}x\\&=- 4 x y - 4 \sin{\left(x + y \right)}+g(y)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, differentiating the above expression with respect to $y,$ we obtain

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂y}=- 4 x - 4 \cos{\left(x + y \right)}+g'(y).
$$

Taking $\frac{∂f}{∂y}=- 4 x - 4 \cos{\left(x + y \right)}$ into account, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}- 4 x - 4 \cos{\left(x + y \right)}+g'(y)&=- 4 x - 4 \cos{\left(x + y \right)}\\g'(y)&=0\\g(y)&=0+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is a constant.

Finally, substituting $g(y)=0+C$ into our expression for $f(x,y),$ we get

$$
f(x,y)=- 4 x y - 4 \sin{\left(x + y \right)}+C.
$$
